_about: Drawings whose values have already been read and written down. When one of these is uploaded, the app fills its values; an engineer still checks, ticks and confirms them. Values are read from the drawing itself and cross-checked against the proven program for the same part. Never invent values. Tolerances not written on a drawing come from that drawing's own general tolerance table.

drawings.title: SLEEVE - 4WD (TAFE), drawing issue 3
drawings.read_by: Read from drawing 3773480M01 issue 3 on 13 Nov 2026; matches proven program O0001
not_in_table: Perpendicularity 0.05 to A, both faces
Concentricity 0.025 of bore to A
Surface finish N6 on OD, N8 elsewhere
Heat treatment: nitrocarburise 3 h at 570 C, min compound layer 12.5 microns on OD (O0001 turns the OD to 44.7)

bar_estimate.note: O0001 rapids at X50 beside the bar (line 34) and cuts it to 45.2 in one pass (lines 41-42): bar between 45.2 and 50, standard size 48.

drawings.back_note: Back end (drawing: 2 x 15 deg chamfers BOTH ENDS on OD and bore). How far the 2nd clamping re-turns the OD (4.0) and bore (5.0) is not on the drawing: taken from O0001 N6 (Z-4.0) and N7 (Z-5.0).

drawings.title: SLEEVE - SUCTION PIPELINE (TAFE), drawing issue 03
drawings.read_by: Read from drawing 3216C11701 issue 03 on 13 Nov 2026; matches proven program O0009
not_in_table: Saddle cut R15.5 at one end (not lathe work)
Cross holes diameter 16.5 and 19.5 (+0.5/-0.2) at 36.5 +-0.8, 7 deg +-1 deg (not lathe work)
OD 25 and bore 19 have no tolerance on the drawing: general tolerance +-0.5 used
Drawing note: refer to the 3D model for any other dimension
CHECK WITH THE PROGRAMMER: O0009 drills 19 only from the saddle end (37 deep); the drawing shows 19 through, so the generated program drills through in the 1st clamping

bar_estimate.note: O0009 rapids at X30 beside the bar (line 8) and turns the OD to 25 in one pass (lines 26-27): bar between 25 and 30, largest standard size below 30 is 28. BUT O0009 turns only 23 mm from one end and 20 mm from the other, so 7 mm of the 50 mm part is never turned: the blank you load is probably already close to D25 there. Measure it.

drawings.back_note: Saddle end (drawing: CH 0.5 x 45 inside). How far the 2nd clamping turns the OD (20.0) and bores (36.5) is not on the drawing: taken from O0009 N2 (Z-20.0) and N4 (Z-36.5).

drawings.title: BOSS-SUCTION PIPE (TAFE), drawing issue 01
drawings.read_by: Read from drawing 3227C07701 issue 01 on 21 Nov 2026; cross-checked with proven program O0003 (3227C07701 BOSS SUC)
not_in_table: Drill D16.5 is not on the drawing: taken from O0003 N1 (Z-40, small end) and N5 (Z-36, flange end)
R3 fillet between D22.22 and the D31 shoulder (O0003 N9/N10: G02 X28.22 Z-34 R3): the table has no inside-corner radius, so the shoulder is drawn sharp

Face groove on the flange face (Detail B): outer D31.88 +-0.25, radial width 3.94 +0.51/0, depth 2.79 +0.13/0, 5 deg walls, R0.2 - the table has no face-groove type; O0003 N8 cuts it with T0808 (3 mm face groove tool)
Perpendicularity 0.05 of the flange face to datum A (bore)
R0.2 max at the flange root; all edges 0.5 x 45 deg (typical)
Finished weight 0.160 kg; coat with long-term rust preventive oil
CHECK WITH THE PROGRAMMER: O0003 N9/N10 turn D30.9 only to Z-56 (11 from the flange face) but the drawing puts the flange (6 thick) at 61 from the small end; the table follows the drawing
CHECK WITH THE PROGRAMMER: O0003 chamfers are 0.75-1.15 x 45 deg (e.g. X20.5 to X19.0 A225) against 0.5 x 45 typical on the drawing; the table follows the drawing
0.5 x 45 chamfer tolerance: the drawing's radii/chamfer table starts above 0.5, so +-0.2 (its smallest row) is used

bar_estimate.note: Not on the drawing. O0003 faces out to X40.5 (N2) and turns the flange down from the bar to X38.5 (N6), and G71 starts at X40 (N9): bright bar 40 (estimate - check the bar in stock).

drawings.back_note: Flange end (2nd OPRN of O0003): face, D38 x 6 flange, bore D19 from this side. The bore is through (D19 +-0.2, 67 long): 33 from the small end (O0003 N3 bores to Z-33) and 34 from the flange end so the two meet.
